areas: Welfare, first aid and ambulance room

questions.q: The OSH&WC Code, 2020 does NOT apply to which of the following?
o: Offices of the Central Government, offices of the State Government and any ship of war
A mine owned by the Government
questions.e: Section 1(3) excludes offices of the Central and State Governments and any ship of war (except contract labour employed there where the Government is principal employer).

questions.q: The Code applies to contract labour employed through a contractor in the offices of the Central Government when:
o: The office has more than 100 employees
The contractor holds a licence for 5 years
The Central Government is the principal employer
questions.e: Proviso to Section 1(3).

questions.q: Under the Code, an "adult" means a person who has completed:
questions.e: Section 2(1)(b): an adult has completed his eighteenth year of age.

questions.q: In relation to a mine, "agent" means:
o: Only a person appointed in writing by the owner
Every person, appointed or not, who acting on behalf of the owner takes part in the management, control, supervision or direction of the mine
The person who receives royalty from the mine
questions.e: Section 2(1)(c).

questions.q: Who is the "appropriate Government" in relation to mines?
o: The State Government with Central approval
The State Government where the mine is located
questions.e: Section 2(1)(d)(i) names mines, oil fields and major ports among establishments for which the Central Government is the appropriate Government.

questions.q: In the case of mines, the term "competent person" specifically also includes:
questions.e: Proviso to Section 2(1)(l): it includes persons authorised by the manager to supervise or perform work, including a shot firer or blaster.

questions.q: Who recognises a "competent person" for carrying out tests, examinations and inspections?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(l).

questions.q: Under the Code, a "day" means:
o: The period between sunrise and sunset
A period of 24 hours beginning at midnight
A period of 24 hours beginning at 6 a.m.
questions.e: Section 2(1)(q).

questions.q: A mine lies partly in District X and partly in District Y. Who is the District Magistrate for the purposes of the Code?
o: The DM of the district with the larger area of the mine
The DM of the district where the mine office is located
The DM authorised in this behalf by the Central Government
questions.e: Proviso to Section 2(1)(r).

questions.q: Which of the following persons is NOT "employed in a mine" under the Code?
o: A person in the mine office
A person servicing machinery used in the mine
A person constructing a road not directly connected with existing or future mining operations
A person loading minerals for dispatch within the mine premises
questions.e: Proviso to Section 2(1)(t)(b) excludes construction of buildings, roads, wells and building work not directly connected with mining operations.

questions.q: A person working under appointment of the mine manager is "employed" in the mine:
o: Only if on the permanent rolls
questions.e: Proviso to Section 2(1)(t): "whether for wages or not".

questions.q: In relation to a mine, "employer" includes:
o: The owner, agent or manager referred to in section 67
questions.e: Section 2(1)(u)(ii).

questions.q: What minimum number of workers makes a mine an "establishment" under the Code?
o: There is no minimum; every mine is an establishment
questions.e: Section 2(1)(v)(iv) covers "a mine" without any worker threshold, unlike sub-clauses (i) and (ii) which require ten or more workers.

questions.q: A premises carrying on a manufacturing process with the aid of power is a "factory" if it employs at least:
questions.e: Section 2(1)(w)(i): 20 or more workers with power, 40 or more without power.

questions.q: A premises carrying on a manufacturing process WITHOUT the aid of power is a "factory" if it employs at least:
questions.e: Section 2(1)(w)(ii).

questions.q: An "inter-State migrant worker" under the Code draws wages not exceeding (or a higher notified amount):
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zf).

questions.q: Which of the following is included in the definition of "mine"?
o: A residential colony of the mine
Power stations supplying electricity solely or mainly for working the mine under the same management
A cement factory near a quarry under different management
A railway siding belonging to Indian Railways
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zl)(ix).

questions.q: Under the definition of "mine", oil wells, borings and the pipe conveying mineral oil within the oilfields are:
o: Included only for oil mines with over 50 workers
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zl)(i).

questions.q: "Minerals" under the Code include:
o: All substances obtainable from the earth by mining, digging, drilling, dredging, quarrying etc., including natural gas and petroleum
Only substances notified by the State
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zm).

questions.q: "Office of the mine" means:
o: An office at the surface of the mine concerned
Any office within 3 km of the mine
The registered office of the company
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zt).

questions.q: An "open cast working" means a quarry, being an excavation that:
o: Is not a shaft or an excavation which extends below superjacent ground
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zu).

questions.q: In the preceding calendar year a mine recorded 75,000 man-days over 300 working days (excluding rest days). How many persons are "ordinarily employed"?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zv): man-days divided by working days = 75,000 / 300 = 250.

questions.q: Which person is NOT an "owner" of a mine under the Code?
o: A person who merely receives a royalty, rent or fine from the mine
A liquidator carrying on the mine's business
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zw).

questions.q: A contractor or sub-lessee for working a mine is:
o: Subject to the Code as if he were an owner, without exempting the owner from liability
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zw).

questions.q: In a mine, the "principal employer" for contract labour is:
o: The owner or agent of the mine
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zz)(iii).

questions.q: A "relay" means:
o: A set of two or more persons carrying out the same kind of work during different periods of the day
A set of workers on overtime
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zzd); each such period is called a "shift".

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a "serious bodily injury" under the Code?
o: Fracture of a bone of a finger
Permanent loss of the use of a hand
A minor bruise that heals in two days
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zzg) covers permanent loss of a body part or its use, permanent loss of or injury to sight or hearing, permanent incapacity, or fracture of any bone or joint, including bones of the phalanges.

questions.q: A "week" under the Code means seven days beginning at midnight on:
o: Saturday night, or another night approved in writing by the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zzk).

questions.q: Which of the following is excluded from the definition of "worker"?
o: A supervisor drawing wages above Rs 18,000 per month (or notified amount)
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zzl)(iv).

questions.q: Which of the following is included in "wages" under the Code?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zzj) includes basic pay, dearness allowance and retaining allowance; HRA, overtime and gratuity are excluded.

questions.q: A worker operates a shovel at the bottom of an opencast pit 90 metres deep. For the purposes of the Code he is employed:
o: Below ground if blasting is done
Below ground, because of the depth
Above ground, because it is an opencast working
Partly below and partly above ground
questions.e: Section 2(2)(b): working in an opencast working is "above ground"; below ground is a shaft being sunk or an excavation extending below superjacent ground.

questions.q: A person working in a shaft that is in the course of being sunk is employed:
questions.e: Section 2(2)(a)(i).

questions.q: An employer of a new establishment to which the Code applies must apply for registration within:
questions.e: Section 3(1).

questions.q: A change in ownership or management after registration must be intimated electronically to the registering officer within:
questions.e: Section 3(4).

questions.q: After the employer informs the closing of an establishment, the registering officer must cancel the registration within:
questions.e: Section 3(5); otherwise it is deemed cancelled and auto-generated.

questions.q: Where registration was obtained fraudulently so that it has become useless, the revocation process must be completed within how many days of the facts coming to notice?
questions.e: Section 3(6).

questions.q: An appeal against an order of the registering officer must be preferred within:
questions.e: Section 4(1); the appellate officer may condone delay for sufficient cause.

questions.q: The appellate officer must dispose of an appeal against a registration order within:
questions.e: Section 4(2).

questions.q: Under Section 5, the notice of commencement and intimation of cessation of operations of a mine must be given:
questions.e: Section 5(2).

questions.q: An employee who had no appointment letter at the commencement of the Code must be issued one within:
questions.e: Section 6(1)(f).

questions.q: Who bears the cost of medical examinations conducted to detect occupational diseases?
o: The employer; no charge may be levied on the employee
questions.e: Section 6(1)(g).

questions.q: Who is jointly and severally responsible for making financial and other provisions for compliance with the Code in a mine?
o: The manager and the safety officer
questions.e: Section 7(1).

questions.q: When a mining provision is contravened, which of the following is NOT deemed guilty along with the contravener (unless due diligence is proved)?
o: The officials appointed to supervise that provision
questions.e: Section 7(2) lists supervising officials, the manager, the owner and agent, and any person appointed under section 24.

questions.q: In proceedings against the owner or agent of a mine under Section 7, which is NOT a valid defence?
o: That reasonable means were taken to prevent the contravention
That the manager and other officials were appointed in accordance with the Code
None of these is a defence
questions.e: Section 7(3).

questions.q: An importer brings in a machine whose country of manufacture uses a higher standard than the Indian standard. Which standard must it conform to?
o: The higher standard of the country of manufacture
questions.e: Proviso (B) to Section 8(1).

questions.q: Under Section 8, an article or substance is NOT regarded as "properly used" when:
o: It is used for more than 8 hours
It is used by a trained worker
It is used without regard to the information or advice made available by its designer, manufacturer, importer or supplier
questions.e: Section 8(7).

questions.q: For the purposes of Section 8, the term "article" includes:
questions.e: Explanation (a) to Section 8.

questions.q: Under Section 9, at what stage must the architect, project engineer or designer give due consideration to the safety and health of building workers?
questions.e: Section 9(1).

questions.q: Under Section 10, notice of an accident is required where it causes death or a bodily injury that prevents the injured person from working for:
o: 48 hours or more immediately following the accident
questions.e: Section 10(1).

questions.q: In a mine, who must send notice of a reportable accident under Section 10?
o: The employer or owner or agent or manager referred to in section 67
questions.e: Section 10(1)(a).

questions.q: For a fatal accident in a building or construction establishment, the authority receiving the notice must make an inquiry within:
questions.e: Section 10(2).

questions.q: Under Section 11, notice of a dangerous occurrence is required:
o: Whether or not it causes bodily injury or disability
questions.e: Section 11.

questions.q: An employer must send notice when a worker contracts a disease specified in which Schedule of the Code?
questions.e: Section 12(1).

questions.q: A qualified medical practitioner who fails to report a Third Schedule disease is liable to a penalty extending to:
questions.e: Section 12(3).

questions.q: A qualified medical practitioner who believes a patient has a Third Schedule disease must send a written report to:
o: The office of the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator
questions.e: Section 12(2).

questions.q: In a mine, an employee noticing an unsafe or unhealthy situation must report it to:
o: The agent or manager referred to in section 67, safety officers, or an official for his workplace
questions.e: Section 13(d).

questions.q: Which of the following is a duty of every employee under Section 13?
o: To take reasonable care for the health and safety of himself and others affected by his acts or omissions
questions.e: Section 13(a).

questions.q: If an employee is not satisfied with the employer's response on inadequate safety provisions, he may represent to:
questions.e: Section 14(1).

questions.q: Workers report imminent danger but the employer is not satisfied that it exists. What must the employer do?
o: Refer it to the Safety Committee for a vote
Refer the matter forthwith to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator, whose decision is final
questions.e: Section 14(4).

questions.q: Section 15 prohibits any person from intentionally or recklessly:
o: Interfering with, damaging or misusing anything provided in the interest of health, safety or welfare
questions.e: Section 15.

questions.q: The National Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board is constituted by:
questions.e: Section 16(1).

questions.q: Who is the ex officio Chairperson of the National Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board?
o: Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Employment
questions.e: Section 16(2)(a).

questions.q: Which mining official is an ex officio member of the National Board?
o: Controller General, Indian Bureau of Mines
questions.e: Section 16(2)(c).

questions.q: Who is the Member Secretary of the National Board?
o: Joint Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Employment
questions.e: Section 16(2)(o).

questions.q: How many representatives each of employers and of employees sit on the National Board?
questions.e: Section 16(2)(j) and (k).

questions.q: How many States' Principal Secretaries (labour) are members of the National Board, by rotation?
questions.e: Section 16(2)(g).

questions.q: The term of office of the nominated members of the National Board is:
questions.e: Section 16(3).

questions.q: Which explosives authority is an ex officio member of the National Board?
questions.e: Section 16(2)(d).

questions.q: The State Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board is constituted by:
questions.e: Section 17(1).

questions.q: Who declares occupational safety and health standards for workplaces such as mines?
questions.e: Section 18(1).

questions.q: Before amending the Second Schedule, the Central Government must notify its intention for not less than:
questions.e: Section 18(3).

questions.q: A State Government may amend the standards for establishments for which it is the appropriate Government:
o: With approval of the High Court
With prior approval of the Central Government
questions.e: Section 18(4).

questions.q: Which authority may conduct a safety and occupational health survey of a mine, among others?
questions.e: Section 20(1)(c); the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator and DG Health Services may also survey mines.

questions.q: Time spent by a worker undergoing medical examination for a survey under Section 20 is:
o: Deemed to be working hours for calculating wages and overtime
questions.e: Section 20(3).

questions.q: An inter-State migrant worker may register on the portal on the basis of:
questions.e: Proviso to Section 21(2).

questions.q: In a Safety Committee constituted under Section 22, the number of workers' representatives must be:
questions.e: Section 22(1).

questions.q: Under the Code, a mine must appoint safety officers when it ordinarily employs at least:
questions.e: Section 22(2)(d).

questions.q: Which establishment needs safety officers at 250 or more workers?
o: Factory carrying on a hazardous process
questions.e: Section 22(2)(b); also building or other construction work with 250 or more.

questions.q: Who prescribes the health, safety and working conditions to be maintained by an employer under Section 23?
questions.e: Section 23(1).

questions.q: Under the Code, canteen facilities are required where how many workers, including contract labourers, are ordinarily employed?
questions.e: Section 24(1)(v).

questions.q: Section 24 specifically provides, in the case of mines, for:
o: Medical examination of employees before employment and at specific intervals
questions.e: Section 24(1)(vi).

questions.q: An ambulance room may be prescribed in every mine wherein more than how many workers are ordinarily employed?
questions.e: Section 24(2)(i).

questions.q: Shelters, rest-rooms and a lunch-room may be prescribed in every mine employing more than:
questions.e: Section 24(2)(iii).

questions.q: A welfare officer is to be appointed in every factory, mine or plantation ordinarily employing:
questions.e: Section 24(2)(iv).

questions.q: Crèche facility is provided for children of employees below the age of:
questions.e: Section 24(3), in establishments with more than 50 workers ordinarily employed.

questions.q: Under Section 25, no worker shall be required or allowed to work for more than:
questions.e: Section 25(1)(a).

questions.q: Who notifies the maximum daily hours for persons employed below ground in a mine?
questions.e: First proviso (i) to Section 25(1).

questions.q: No person employed in a mine may be present below ground except:
o: During the periods of work shown for him in the register under section 33(a)
questions.e: First proviso (iii) to Section 25(1).

questions.q: Work below ground in a mine must be carried on by:
o: A system of shifts so arranged that each shift is not spread over more than the notified daily maximum
questions.e: First proviso (ii) to Section 25(1).

questions.q: No worker shall be allowed to work in an establishment for more than how many days in any one week?
questions.e: Section 26(1).

questions.q: A worker deprived of weekly holidays due to an exemption must get compensatory holidays:
o: At the end of the year
Within the month the holidays were due or the two months immediately following
questions.e: Section 26(3).

questions.q: Overtime is paid at what rate under the Code?
o: One and a half times the wages
questions.e: Section 27.

questions.q: Overtime is calculated on a daily or weekly basis:
o: Whichever is more favourable to the worker
questions.e: Section 27.

questions.q: Under the first proviso to Section 27, a worker may be required to work overtime:
o: Subject to the consent of the worker
questions.e: First proviso to Section 27.

questions.q: A miner's night shift runs from 10 p.m. Monday to 6 a.m. Tuesday. For him, the "following day" begins:
o: At 6 a.m. Tuesday, when the shift ends; hours worked after midnight count in Monday
questions.e: Section 28(b).

questions.q: Can the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator exempt a mine from the prohibition on overlapping shifts?
o: No; the exemption power does not apply to mines
Yes, with the State Government's approval
questions.e: Proviso to Section 29(2).

questions.q: No worker may work in a mine if he has already worked in another similar establishment within the preceding:
questions.e: Section 30 (restriction on double employment in factory and mine).

questions.q: Without the previous sanction of the Inspector-cum-Facilitator, a change in the notice of periods of work cannot be made until how long after the last change?
questions.e: Section 31(3).

questions.q: To be entitled to annual leave with wages, a worker must have worked in the calendar year at least:
questions.e: Section 32(1)(i).

questions.q: A worker employed below ground in a mine earns one day of annual leave for every:
questions.e: Section 32(1)(ii): 1 per 20 days generally, 1 per 15 for adolescents and below-ground mine workers.

questions.q: A below-ground miner works 270 days in a calendar year. How many days of annual leave with wages does he earn?
questions.e: Section 32(1)(ii): 270 / 15 = 18 days.

questions.q: A surface worker in a mine works 240 days in a calendar year. How many days of annual leave does he earn?
questions.e: Section 32(1)(ii): 240 / 20 = 12 days.

questions.q: A worker who joins on a date other than 1 January is entitled to leave if he has worked for what part of the remaining days of the year?
questions.e: Section 32(1)(v).

questions.q: The maximum unavailed leave that can be carried forward to the next calendar year (excluding leave refused) is:
questions.e: Section 32(1)(vii)(a).

questions.q: Leave that a worker applied for but was refused can be carried forward:
questions.e: Section 32(1)(vii)(b).

questions.q: Where a worker quits employment, wages in lieu of leave must be paid before the expiry of:
questions.e: Section 32(1)(vi)(a); on superannuation or death, within two months.

questions.q: On a worker's death in service, wages in lieu of leave must be paid to his heir or nominee within:
questions.e: Section 32(1)(vi)(b).

questions.q: Periods of lay-off, maternity leave or annual leave during the year are:
o: Counted towards the 180 days, but leave is not earned for them
Counted and leave is earned for them
questions.e: Section 32(1)(iii).

questions.q: If an award or contract gives a mine worker longer annual leave than Section 32(1), then:
o: The longer leave under the award or contract applies
questions.e: Proviso to Section 32(3).

questions.q: Working journalists may work a maximum of how many hours in any four consecutive weeks?
questions.e: Section 25(2).

questions.q: Under Section 33, the register of workers maintained by an employer must include particulars of:
o: Work performed, normal hours, rest day, wages, leave, overtime, attendance, dangerous occurrences and employment of adolescents
questions.e: Section 33(a).

questions.q: Under Section 33, wage slips must be issued to workers:
questions.e: Section 33(c).

questions.q: A Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator may be appointed for:
o: A State, more than one State, or the whole country
questions.e: Proviso to Section 34(5).

questions.q: Which person cannot be appointed or continue as an Inspector-cum-Facilitator?
o: A person directly or indirectly interested in a workplace or business carried on there
A person with an engineering degree
questions.e: Section 34(8).

questions.q: Inspector-cum-Facilitators are deemed to be public servants within the meaning of:
o: Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code
questions.e: Section 34(11).

questions.q: Under the inspection scheme, the unique number given to each establishment is the same as its:
questions.e: Section 34(4)(a).

questions.q: The inspection scheme under Section 34 may provide for:
o: Randomised selection of establishments and Inspector-cum-Facilitators, and web-based inspection
questions.e: Section 34(3).

questions.q: Which is a power of an Inspector-cum-Facilitator under Section 35?
o: Directing that premises be left undisturbed for an inspection or inquiry
questions.e: Section 35(1)(viii).

questions.q: An Inspector-cum-Facilitator may take samples of:
o: Any articles or substances in the establishment and the air in or near it
questions.e: Section 35(1)(x).

questions.q: A person required by an Inspector-cum-Facilitator to produce a document is deemed legally bound to do so within the meaning of:
questions.e: Section 35(2).

questions.q: A search or seizure by an Inspector-cum-Facilitator is governed by the CrPC provisions applicable to a warrant under:
questions.e: Section 35(3).

questions.q: Who prescribes the powers and duties of an Inspector-cum-Facilitator that the District Magistrate may exercise in respect of mines?
questions.e: Section 36.

questions.q: Under Section 37, experts for third-party audit and certification are assigned:
o: In a randomised manner through a web-based scheme
questions.e: Section 37(2)(a).

questions.q: If a matter in a mine is dangerous and no express provision covers it, the Inspector-cum-Facilitator may:
o: Give written notice requiring it to be remedied within a specified time and manner
Fine the owner on the spot
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(a).

questions.q: If the employer does not comply with a notice under Section 38(1)(B)(a), the Inspector-cum-Facilitator may:
o: Prohibit employment of any person not reasonably necessary for securing compliance
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(b).

questions.q: An Inspector-cum-Facilitator may prohibit the extraction or reduction of pillars if it is likely to cause:
o: Crushing of pillars or premature collapse of workings, or if fire or flooding precautions are inadequate
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(c).

questions.q: Where there is urgent and immediate danger to life in a mine, the prohibition order lasts:
o: Until the Inspector is satisfied the danger is removed
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(d).

questions.q: A person whose employment is prohibited under Section 38(1)(B)(b) or (d) is entitled to:
o: Full wages, or alternative employment at the same wages
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(e).

questions.q: The employer of a mine may appeal against a notice or order of an Inspector-cum-Facilitator under Section 38(1)(B) to the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator within:
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(f).

questions.q: An employer objecting to a notice or order may send a written objection to the Central Government within:
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(h).

questions.q: The Central Government ordinarily decides an objection under Section 38(1)(B)(h) within:
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(h).

questions.q: While an objection is pending with the Central Government, the notice or order:
o: Must be complied with, though the Central Government may suspend a notice under (a) on application
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(i).

questions.q: An Inspector-cum-Facilitator who issues a notice or prohibitory order in a mine must forthwith report it to:
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(g).

questions.q: Who is liable to pay full wages to persons whose employment is prohibited under Section 38(1)(B)(l)?
o: The owner, agent or manager referred to in section 67
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(m).

questions.q: Before an order prejudicial to the owner, agent or manager is made under Section 38, they must be:
o: Given a reasonable opportunity of making representation
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(p).

questions.q: Who may reverse or modify an order passed by the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator in relation to a mine?
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(q).

questions.q: An Inspector-cum-Facilitator's prohibitory order for a factory under imminent danger has effect for:
o: Three days, unless extended by the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator
questions.e: Section 38(1)(A)(b).

questions.q: Section 38 does not affect the powers of a magistrate under:
o: Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
questions.e: Section 38(1)(B)(j).

questions.q: Information acquired by an Inspector-cum-Facilitator during inspection is:
o: Confidential, unless disclosure is necessary for the health, safety or welfare of employees
questions.e: Section 39(1).

questions.q: Which mining authority may receive confidential inspection information without breaching Section 39?
o: The Controller, Indian Bureau of Mines
questions.e: Section 39(2)(e).

questions.q: Notwithstanding the RTI Act, an Inspector-cum-Facilitator must not disclose, without consent:
questions.e: Section 39(3).

questions.q: Under Section 40, every employer must afford Inspectors-cum-Facilitators:
o: A copy of the balance sheet
All reasonable facilities for entry, inspection, survey, measurement, examination or inquiry
questions.e: Section 40.

questions.q: A government servant authorised to survey, level or measure a mine must give the manager notice of at least:
questions.e: Section 41; no notice is needed in an emergency, by written order.

questions.q: Which is NOT a duty of a medical officer under Section 42?
o: Granting a Manager's Certificate of Competency
Medical supervision where illness appears due to the work
Certifying an adolescent's fitness for employment
Examining and certifying workers in a mine in prescribed dangerous occupations
questions.e: Section 42(2).

questions.q: Before entering office, a medical officer appointed under Section 42 must disclose:
o: His interest in the concerned establishment
questions.e: Proviso to Section 42(1).

questions.q: Under Section 43, women may be employed before 6 a.m. and beyond 7 p.m.:
o: With their consent, subject to prescribed conditions
Only with DGMS permission in each case
questions.e: Section 43.

questions.q: Under Section 43, women are entitled to be employed in:
o: All establishments for all types of work
questions.e: Section 43.

questions.q: Where employment of women in an operation is dangerous, Section 44 empowers the appropriate Government to:
o: Require the employer to provide adequate safeguards before employing women
questions.e: Section 44.

questions.q: Part I (contract labour) of Chapter XI applies to every establishment employing, on any day of the preceding 12 months, at least:
questions.e: Section 45(1).

questions.q: Work is NOT deemed intermittent if it was performed in the preceding 12 months for more than:
questions.e: Explanation to Section 45(2); for seasonal work, more than 60 days in a year.

questions.q: A contractor's licence under Section 47(1) is valid for:
questions.e: Section 48(3).

questions.q: Under Section 49, a contractor may charge contract labour:
o: No fee or commission at all
questions.e: Section 49.

questions.q: A contractor who does not meet the licence criteria may be issued:
o: A "work specific licence" for the concerned work order
questions.e: Section 47(2).

questions.q: An appeal against an order on a contractor's licence must be filed within:
questions.e: Section 52(1); it is disposed of within 30 days.

questions.q: Who must provide the welfare facilities under Sections 23 and 24 to contract labour?
questions.e: Section 53.

questions.q: Employing contract labour through a contractor who must hold a licence but does not is:
o: Deemed a contravention of the Code
questions.e: Section 54.

questions.q: A contractor fails to pay wages to contract labour in a mine within the prescribed period. Who must pay?
o: The principal employer, who may recover it from the contractor
questions.e: Section 55(3).

questions.q: A contractor must disburse wages to contract labour:
o: Through bank transfer or electronic mode, informing the principal employer
questions.e: Section 55(2).

questions.q: An experience certificate must be issued to contract labour by:
questions.e: Section 56.

questions.q: Employment of contract labour in core activities of an establishment is:

questions.q: How does the OSH&WC Code, 2020 come into force?
o: Ninety days after publication in the Gazette
On the date the President gives assent
On dates appointed by the Central Government by notification, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions
questions.e: Section 1(2): the Code comes into force on such date as the Central Government may appoint by notification, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions.

questions.q: The Code takes the meaning of "adolescent" from which Act?
o: The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986
questions.e: Section 2(1)(a): "adolescent" has the meaning in clause (i) of section 2 of the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986.

questions.q: For a Central Public Sector Undertaking, the Central Government remains the appropriate Government even if its equity holding falls below:
questions.e: Proviso to Section 2(1)(d)(i): it continues to be the Central Government even if its holding reduces to less than fifty per cent equity.

questions.q: Who is the appropriate Government for occupational safety, health and working conditions in a factory?
o: The Directorate General of Mines Safety
The State Government in which the factory is situated
questions.e: Explanation to Section 2(1)(d): the State Government is the appropriate Government in respect of OSH and working conditions in a factory situated in that State.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT listed as an establishment for which the Central Government is the appropriate Government?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(d)(ii): plantations, factories, motor transport undertakings, newspaper establishments and beedi and cigar establishments come under the State Government.

questions.q: Which of the following is included in "audio-visual production"?
o: Web-based serials, talk shows, reality shows and sport shows
questions.e: Section 2(1)(e) includes animation, advertisements, digital production, feature and non-feature films, television, web-based serials, talk shows, reality shows and sport shows.

questions.q: Building or other construction work for an individual's own residence is excluded from the definition if its total cost does not exceed (or a higher notified amount):
questions.e: Section 2(1)(h): own residential work costing not more than rupees fifty lakhs (or a higher notified amount) is excluded.

questions.q: Which construction work is specifically excluded from "building or other construction work"?
o: Construction work related to any factory or mine
questions.e: Section 2(1)(h) excludes building or other construction work which is related to any factory or mine.

questions.q: Who is NOT a "building worker" under the Code?
o: A clerk on a construction site
A person employed mainly in a managerial or supervisory capacity
questions.e: Section 2(1)(i) excludes any person employed mainly in a managerial, supervisory or administrative capacity.

questions.q: Under the Code, "cargo" includes anything carried or to be carried in:
o: A ship or other vessel, or vehicle
questions.e: Section 2(1)(j): "cargo" includes anything carried or to be carried in a ship or other vessel, or vehicle.

questions.q: The Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator is appointed under which provision of the Code?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(k): the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator is appointed under sub-section (5) of section 34.

questions.q: "Contract labour" under the Code includes:
o: Only workers hired with the knowledge of the principal employer
Workers hired through a contractor with or without the knowledge of the principal employer, including inter-State migrant workers
Only permanent employees of the contractor
questions.e: Section 2(1)(m): contract labour is hired by or through a contractor with or without the knowledge of the principal employer and includes inter-State migrant workers.

questions.q: Does the definition of "contractor" include a sub-contractor?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(n): "contractor" includes a sub-contractor.

questions.q: A person who merely supplies goods or articles of manufacture to an establishment is:
o: Not a contractor for that supply
questions.e: Section 2(1)(n)(i): undertaking to produce a result through contract labour is covered, other than a mere supply of goods or articles of manufacture.

questions.q: A "controlled industry" is one whose control by the Central Government has been declared:
o: Under any Central Act in the public interest
questions.e: Section 2(1)(o).

questions.q: Which of these is NOT treated as an essential part of a core activity when the establishment is not set up for it?
o: Mining of the mineral for which the mine is worked
Watch and ward services including security services
questions.e: Proviso to Section 2(1)(p) lists sanitation, watch and ward (including security), canteen, loading and unloading and other support services.

questions.q: An activity of intermittent nature that constitutes a core activity of an establishment is:
o: Not to be considered an essential or necessary activity
questions.e: Proviso clause (xi) to Section 2(1)(p).

questions.q: Under the Code, "dock work" includes:
o: Only loading and unloading of cargo
Ship building in a shipyard factory
Chipping, painting or cleaning of any hold, tank, structure or lifting machinery on board the ship or in the docks
questions.e: Section 2(1)(s)(iii).

questions.q: Which person is excluded from "employee" in respect of an establishment?
o: An apprentice engaged under the Apprentices Act, 1961
questions.e: Section 2(1)(t)(i) excludes apprentices engaged under the Apprentices Act, 1961; members of the Armed Forces are also excluded.

questions.q: A person doing watch and ward within the mine premises, but in the residential area, is:
o: Not employed in the mine for this purpose
questions.e: Proviso clause (f) to Section 2(1)(t) covers watch and ward within the premises of the mine excluding residential area.

questions.q: A person loading minerals for dispatch within the premises of a mine is:
o: Employed only if paid daily wages
questions.e: Proviso clause (d) to Section 2(1)(t).

questions.q: For an establishment carried on by a local authority, the "employer" is:
o: The Chief Executive of that authority
questions.e: Section 2(1)(u).

questions.q: Which of these is included in "employer"?
o: The legal representative of a deceased employer
questions.e: Section 2(1)(u)(v).

questions.q: An industry, trade or business becomes an "establishment" when it employs at least:
questions.e: Section 2(1)(v)(i): ten or more workers; a mine or port is an establishment regardless of numbers.

questions.q: The worker threshold for an establishment does not apply where:
o: A hazardous or life-threatening activity notified by the Central Government is carried on
The establishment is in a city
questions.e: First proviso to Section 2(1)(v).

questions.q: Which of these is excluded from the definition of "factory"?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(w) excludes mobile units of the armed forces, railways running sheds and hotels, restaurants or eating places.

questions.q: When counting workers to decide whether premises are a factory:
o: Only workers using power are counted
Only the largest shift is counted
All workers in different groups and relays in a day are counted
questions.e: Explanation I to Section 2(1)(w).

questions.q: Premises where only a computer unit is installed and no manufacturing process is carried on are:
o: A factory if 20 persons work there
questions.e: Explanation II to Section 2(1)(w).

questions.q: For a worker, "family" includes dependent children who have not completed the age of:
questions.e: Section 2(1)(x)(ii).

questions.q: Which of these dependants is included in a worker's "family"?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(x)(iii): parents, grand-parents, widowed daughter and widowed sister dependent on the worker.

questions.q: Under the Code, "hazardous" means:
questions.e: Section 2(1)(z).

questions.q: A "hazardous process" relates to an industry or plantation specified in:
questions.e: Section 2(1)(za).

questions.q: Which activity is excluded from the definition of "industry"?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zd) excludes charitable institutions, sovereign functions (defence research, atomic energy, space), domestic service and notified activities.

questions.q: Activities of Central Government departments dealing with which of these are excluded from "industry" as sovereign functions?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zd)(b): defence research, atomic energy and space.

questions.q: "Machinery" under the Code is anything used or intended to be used for:
o: Converting any form of energy to perform work
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zg).

questions.q: Which of these is a "manufacturing process" under the Code?
o: Preserving or storing any article in cold storage
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zi)(vi).

questions.q: Workshops within the precincts of a mine form part of the "mine" if they are:
o: Under the same management and used primarily for purposes connected with that mine or mines
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zl)(viii).

questions.q: Premises used for depositing sand for use in a mine are part of the mine when:
o: They are exclusively occupied by the owner of the mine
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zl)(x).

questions.q: Are conveyors and aerial ropeways that remove refuse from a mine included in the definition of "mine"?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zl)(v).

questions.q: Which method of obtaining substances is expressly listed in the definition of "minerals"?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zm): mining, digging, drilling, dredging, hydraulicing, quarrying or any other operation.

questions.q: Which person is included in "motor transport worker"?
o: A person employed in a factory
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zo) includes driver, conductor, cleaner, station staff, booking clerk, time-keeper and watchman.

questions.q: In a company, who can be the "occupier" of a factory?
o: Any one of the directors, except an independent director
questions.e: Proviso (ii) to Section 2(1)(zs).

questions.q: When a ship is repaired in a dry dock available for hire, who is generally the occupier?
questions.e: Second proviso to Section 2(1)(zs).

questions.q: Land growing tea, coffee, rubber, cinchona or cardamom is a "plantation" if it admeasures at least:
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zx)(a)(i).

questions.q: In a factory, the "principal employer" for contract labour is:
o: The owner or occupier, or the person named as manager
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zz)(ii).

questions.q: Each period of work of a relay is called a:
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zzd).

questions.q: The fracture of a bone of a finger phalanx is:
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zzg) includes the fracture of any bone or one or more joints or bones of any phalanges of hand or foot.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT part of "wages" under the Code?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zzj): wages include basic pay, DA and retaining allowance; HRA is excluded.

questions.q: If excluded payments exceed what share of total remuneration, the excess is added back to wages?
questions.e: First proviso to Section 2(1)(zzj): one-half or another notified percentage.

questions.q: Remuneration in kind is treated as wages up to what share of total wages?
questions.e: Explanation to Section 2(1)(zzj).

questions.q: Which of these is included in "worker" under the Code?
o: A person employed mainly in managerial capacity
A person subject to the Army Act
Working journalists and sales promotion employees
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zzl).

questions.q: Which of these is included in "working journalist"?
questions.e: Section 2(1)(zzm) includes editor, reporter, correspondent, cartoonist, news-photographer and proof-reader.

questions.q: An application for registration of an establishment under Section 3 is made:
o: To the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator by registered post
On paper to the District Magistrate
Electronically to the registering officer appointed by the appropriate Government
questions.e: Section 3(1).

questions.q: Can the registering officer accept a registration application after the 60-day period?
o: Yes, on payment of the prescribed late fees
questions.e: Proviso to Section 3(1).

questions.q: The registration application must include information relating to the employment of:
questions.e: Section 3(2).

questions.q: If the registering officer fails to register an establishment within the prescribed period:
o: The establishment is deemed registered and the electronic certificate is auto-generated
questions.e: Proviso to Section 3(3); responsibility for the failure lies on the registering officer.

questions.q: Within how many days of closing an establishment must the employer inform the registering officer and certify payment of all dues to workers?
questions.e: Section 3(5).

questions.q: If the registering officer does not cancel the registration within 60 days after closure information, the registration:
o: Must be cancelled by the appellate officer
Is deemed cancelled and the cancellation is auto-generated
questions.e: Proviso to Section 3(5).

questions.q: Where registration was obtained by misrepresentation or suppression of a material fact, what follows under Section 3(6)?
o: The registration is cancelled at once
It is treated as a contravention for prosecution under section 94, without affecting the registration and running of the establishment
A fine of Rs 1 lakh is imposed by the registering officer
questions.e: Section 3(6)(a).

questions.q: An employer whose establishment is not registered under Section 3:
o: Shall not employ any employee in the establishment
questions.e: Section 3(7).

questions.q: An existing establishment already registered under any Central labour law is:
o: Deemed registered under the Code if it provides its registration details within the prescribed time
questions.e: Section 3(8).

questions.q: An appeal against an order under Section 3 lies to:
o: An appellate officer notified by the appropriate Government
questions.e: Section 4(1).

questions.q: Can the appellate officer hear an appeal filed after 30 days?
o: Yes, if satisfied the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause
questions.e: Proviso to Section 4(1).

questions.q: Section 5 requires notice of commencement and cessation of operation from which establishments?
o: Factory, mine, contract labour and building or other construction work establishments
questions.e: Section 5(1).

questions.q: Under Section 6, the employer must ensure that the workplace is free from hazards which cause or are likely to cause:
o: Injury or occupational disease to employees
questions.e: Section 6(1)(a).

questions.q: Annual health examination provided by the employer under Section 6 is:
o: Free of cost to the prescribed classes of employees
questions.e: Section 6(1)(c).

questions.q: Which disposal duty is expressly placed on the employer by Section 6?
o: Disposal of domestic garbage of workers
Disposal of hazardous and toxic waste including e-waste
questions.e: Section 6(1)(e).

questions.q: In a mine, the employer is responsible for the safety and health of persons on the work premises:
questions.e: Section 6(1)(h) covers employees, workers and other persons on the premises, with or without his knowledge.

questions.q: Which of these is a particular duty of the employer in mines under Section 6(2)?
o: Providing information, instruction, training and supervision necessary for health and safety
questions.e: Section 6(2)(c).

questions.q: Section 6(2) requires the employer to maintain safe means of:
o: Access to and egress from places of work
questions.e: Section 6(2)(d).

questions.q: Under Section 7(2), the person appointed to carry out the responsibility under which section is also deemed guilty of a contravention?
questions.e: Section 7(2)(d).

questions.q: A person deemed guilty under Section 7(2) can escape liability by proving that he:
o: Used due diligence to secure compliance and took reasonable means to prevent the contravention
questions.e: Section 7(2).

questions.q: If no Indian standard exists for an imported article, it must conform to:
o: The national standard of the country from which it is imported
The standard fixed by the importer
questions.e: Proviso (C) to Section 8(1).

questions.q: Additional duties of designers, manufacturers, importers and suppliers are specified by the Central Government by regulations in consultation with:
o: The National Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board
questions.e: Section 8(2).

questions.q: Must a supplier repeat testing already carried out by someone else?
o: No, so far as it is reasonable to rely on those results
questions.e: Section 8(4).

questions.q: Duties of designers and manufacturers under Section 8(1) and (2) extend to:
o: Things done in the course of their business and matters within their control
questions.e: Section 8(5).

questions.q: For Section 8, "substance" means a natural or artificial substance in the form of:
questions.e: Explanation (b) to Section 8.

questions.q: Under Section 9(2), architects and project engineers must take care not to include in the design:
o: Dangerous structures or processes or materials hazardous to the health or safety of workers
questions.e: Section 9(2).

questions.q: Section 9(3) requires designers to take into account the safety aspects of:
o: The maintenance and upkeep of the structures and buildings
questions.e: Section 9(3).

questions.q: In a factory or dock work establishment, who sends notice of an accident under Section 10?
questions.e: Section 10(1)(b).

questions.q: If there is no authority to inquire into a fatal accident in a building or construction establishment, who causes the inquiry?
o: The Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator, through an Inspector-cum-Facilitator
questions.e: Section 10(2).

questions.q: Under Section 13, an employee must not wilfully interfere with or misuse:
o: Any appliance or thing provided for securing health, safety and welfare of workers
questions.e: Section 13(e).

questions.q: Which is a duty of the employee under Section 13?
o: To pay for personal protective equipment
To co-operate with the employer in meeting the employer's statutory obligations under the Code
questions.e: Section 13(c).

questions.q: In an establishment other than a mine, an employee who notices an unsafe situation reports it to:
o: His employer or the health and safety representative
questions.e: Section 13(d).

questions.q: Under Section 14(1), an employee may represent about inadequate safety provisions to the employer:
o: Only in writing through a lawyer
Directly or through a member of the Safety Committee
questions.e: Section 14(1).

questions.q: An employee who apprehends imminent serious injury or death may bring it to the notice of the employer and simultaneously to:
questions.e: Section 14(2).

questions.q: When the employer is satisfied that an imminent danger exists, he must take immediate remedial action and send a report forthwith to:
questions.e: Section 14(3).

questions.q: Which of these is a function of the National Board?
o: Advising the Central Government on standards, rules and regulations under the Code
questions.e: Section 16(1)(a).

questions.q: Which officer from Mumbai is an ex officio member of the National Board?
o: Director General, Factory Advice Service and Labour Institutes
questions.e: Section 16(2)(b).
